notes: For the architect, and the reason this round is not simply clean. `envoy-go-race` is red at 6fc96db1 — but not for round 1's reason, which is fixed. It is red on `--- FAIL: TestAStuckDeliveryStillEndsTheKVWatchers` (packages/envoy/internal/bus/drain_hook_edges_test.go:249, `the drain logged "WARN envoy nats reconnect attempt failed", want nothing`), in `internal/bus`, a package this branch does not touch at all (`git diff 88840d35c5fd d5669e82 -- packages/envoy/internal/bus/` is empty). It passed in this branch's own round-1 race job (`ok … /internal/bus 393.846s`), and I ran it 12 times under `-race` in the pod without a failure. The test asserts that a 3 s drain against a real NATS logs no warning, which is timing-sensitive on a lane running six packages at once. I tried to reproduce it under CPU contention, starved this 2-core pod and had to abandon that line. So: a flaky test outside this tree, whose fix is not clear (whether a reconnect attempt during a drain is a product defect or an assertion that should tolerate it is the question commit d4cbcfe6e, '#2396', was about). It is not mine to fix here and not an issue I file; it is yours to decide.

What makes it worth your attention rather than a footnote: main consolidated its CI into `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` while this branch was in review, and a pull request's checks come from the merge ref, so this branch now runs main's new workflow. That workflow ends in a `ci-ok` job whose own script says it is 'the one check main's ruleset requires of the router' and which fails when any selected job fails, with `envoy-go-race` among its `needs` (ci.yaml:2271 defines the lane with the same `go test -race -timeout 30m` step at :2304, so my timing arithmetic still applies; ci.yaml lists it under ci-ok's needs at :2750). Reading main's ruleset right now still gives `["lint","typecheck","test","pr-title"]` and not `ci-ok`, so the two disagree and I cannot say from here which governs the merge. If `ci-ok` is or becomes the required check, a red `envoy-go-race` blocks this pull request however unrelated its cause, which is not what I recorded in round 2 when the lane was merely advisory.

A second consequence of that consolidation, for the merger rather than for this round: `typecheck` is now `needs: changes` behind a path filter (ci.yaml), and at f009ee1a — whose only change is a YAML fragment — it is `skipped` while it was `success` at 6fc96db1 and 612648e7. It is one of the four contexts main's ruleset requires. Whether GitHub counts a skipped required check as satisfied I did not establish: no pull request among the last 25 merged carries a skipped `typecheck`, since the filter is new. Retro's head will be another such head, since retro touches `.legion/` and `docs/solutions/` alone. Worth knowing before READY.
